name: vix_regime_switch_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when India VIX is elevated above its 60-minute session rolling mean by more than 1.5 standard deviations and begins declining (negative 60-second VIX slope), market makers and institutional hedgers start unwinding their defensive put positions — this unwind creates aggressive spot buying that drives 30-50 NIFTY point bounces over the next 30-90 seconds. The inverse holds: when VIX is depressed below session baseline and starts rising, fresh hedging demand enters the options market, and dealers delta-hedge by selling NIFTY futures, pushing spot down. VIX re-prices faster than spot (it is derived from option bid-ask midpoints), giving a 5-10 second lead on directional moves in the index.

indicators.name: vix_zscore
indicators.purpose: 720 bars = 60 minutes captures the intraday session VIX baseline. The original used 20-day daily BB which requires EOD data. For intraday 5s bars, 60 minutes is the right context window — it captures the current session's volatility regime without contaminating with the previous day's VIX level. Shorter windows (e.g., 10 min / 120 bars) are too noisy; longer windows (e.g., 3h) are too slow to update when regime changes mid-session.

indicators.name: vix_slope_12
indicators.purpose: 12 bars = 60 seconds detects VIX turning direction at the precision needed for a 30-120s hold. The original used vix_change_60 on 1-min bars (= 60-minute VIX change) which is far too slow for our hold time. At 5s resolution, a 60-second VIX slope is the minimum reliable slope estimate — shorter (e.g., 3 bars / 15s) is too noisy as VIX ticks irregularly.

indicators.name: ret_6
indicators.purpose: 30-second NIFTY return as directional guard. Replaces the original's nifty_return_60 (60-min bars x 60 = 60-minute return). For a 30-120s trade, we need confirmation that the index is not already in a violent one-directional move when the VIX signal fires — 30s return is sufficient to detect this without being so long that it becomes redundant with the VIX signal itself.

conditions: vix_zscore > vix_zscore_high (VIX is elevated vs session mean — fear regime active)
vix_slope_12 < -vix_slope_thresh (VIX turning down — hedgers starting to unwind puts)
ret_6 > -0.002 (NIFTY not in freefall — guards against genuine crash where VIX dip is a false start)
buy_ce.confirmation: All three conditions simultaneously: elevated VIX context + VIX directional turn + NIFTY not already crashing

conditions: vix_zscore < -vix_zscore_low (VIX below session mean — complacency regime)
vix_slope_12 > vix_slope_thresh (VIX starting to rise — fresh hedging demand building)
ret_6 < 0.002 (NIFTY not in melt-up — guards against continuation gaps where VIX rise is brief)
buy_pe.confirmation: All three conditions simultaneously: depressed VIX context + VIX starting to climb + NIFTY not already surging

exit.stop_rationale: NIFTY VIX-driven bounces average 30-50 spot points over 60-90 seconds (~4-7 option pts at delta 0.5). A 4-point stop means the trade fails if NIFTY moves 8 spot points against the thesis within the hold window — if VIX truly turned but NIFTY continues against, the regime read was wrong and cutting fast preserves capital.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points corresponds to ~14 spot points on NIFTY at delta 0.5. VIX-driven directional unwinding on NIFTY typically produces 30-50 spot point moves in the first 60-90 seconds; 14 spot points is ~40% of the median expected move, giving 1:1.75 R:R while staying within a realistic 2-minute hold window.

filters.vix_filter: core to strategy — VIX z-score threshold defines the regime; 720-bar session rolling window
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST — skip first 15 minutes (VIX stabilizes after pre-open noise) and last 10 minutes
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume is noisy at 5s; VIX slope is the primary filter
filters.trend_filter: ret_6 directional guard prevents entries into existing strong moves
filters.spread_filter: N/A — limit orders at candle close, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VIX mean reversion is structural; option dealer delta-hedging mechanics are persistent and not easily arbed away at 5s granularity

adaptation_notes: Three major changes from original: (1) Universe shifted from high-beta Nifty50 stocks to NIFTY index options — eliminates stock-specific execution risk and spread issues; all the VIX thesis is really about index dynamics anyway. (2) 20-day daily Bollinger Band replaced by 60-minute intraday rolling z-score — the original's 20-day BB requires EOD data and is too slow to update intraday; 60-minute session context captures VIX regime shifts that actually occur intraday. (3) Hold time compressed from 60-180 minutes to 30-120 seconds — the first leg of a VIX-driven NIFTY bounce/fall happens in the first 30-90 seconds as the fastest participants (market makers, gamma hedgers) react; we only need to capture this initial leg, not the full recovery which the original held for.
weaknesses: VIX z-score requires 60-minute warmup (720 bars) — no signals in first hour of session
VIX can turn briefly without NIFTY following — short-term VIX wiggles on noise generate false signals during low-vol sessions
During genuine crises (VIX spiking continuously), the turning-down signal may fire repeatedly as VIX makes lower highs but overall continues climbing — multiple whipsaw losses possible
